Ordering empty shoe boxes

Not every pair arrives with a box worth selling. Some come crushed; some come with none at all. So we buy empty boxes from the same suppliers, on the same paperwork as the shoes. This is the whole loop — PH raises the order, the supplier declares and ships it, the warehouse counts it in and finally puts a box on a pair. Steps 1–7 are PH and the supplier; steps 8–12 are the warehouse.

PHOpen the order
as an empty boxes order
SUPPLIERDeclare each box
SKU, size, carton, cost
SUPPLIERClose & ship
print the manifest, attach, ship
WAREHOUSECount it in
against the same list
WAREHOUSEPut one on a pair
from the No Box queue
The one rule worth learning first A box is identified by three things: the SKU of the shoe it belongs to, the size it was made for, and its dimensions. All three are required. A size 9 box and a size 10 box of the same shoe are two different things to order — even when they measure the same — because the label printed on each box says which size it is. Everything else in this document follows from that.
1PH: open the order as an empty-boxes order
  1. Go to New Batch (Purchase Order), as you would for shoes.
  2. Under What is this order for? tap Empty shoe boxes. The line under it changes to tell you what the supplier will be asked for.
  3. Pick the supplier account, add the tag/code and the shipping labels, and create it.
The choice sits at the top of the form because it changes what the supplier is asked to declare.
Leave it on Shoes unless you mean it Every order defaults to Shoes, and an order raised before this feature existed stays a shoes order. Nothing changes for them.
2PH: already raised it as shoes? Change it

This happens constantly — the order goes in before anyone says what it is for. It is fixable, and the supplier cannot declare anything until it is fixed.

  1. Open the order from Purchase Orders.
  2. Tap Edit details.
  3. Switch What is this order for? to Empty shoe boxes and Save details.
The same choice, on an order that already exists.
Change it before anything is declared Lines already entered are kept, but a shoe line's size and a box line's dimensions are different facts — so anything declared under the old kind comes back blank and has to be re-stated. The order's thread records who changed it and when.
A settled order will not change Once an order is reconciled or archived, its count has been agreed with the supplier and nothing about it can be edited — the kind included.
3Supplier: open your order and check the chip
  1. Sign in to the supplier portal and tap Purchase Orders.
  2. Open the order you are packing.
  3. Look for the Empty boxes chip beside the status. If it says Shoes instead, stop and ask us to change it — you will not be able to enter dimensions until we do.
The chip appears on the list and on the order. The note under it says what you are being asked for.

What every box needs

Four facts. Miss one and the box cannot be checked off when it reaches us.

FieldWhat to put in itWhy we ask
SKUThe style code printed on the box — e.g. DD1391-100.It is how the box is matched to the shoe that needs it.
Shoe nameFills in from the SKU. Type it if the lookup cannot find it.So a person reading the sheet knows what they are holding.
SizeThe size on the box's own label — not the size of the shoe you have spare.A size 9 box only fits a size 9. This is the field that decides the box is useful.
DimensionsOutside length × width × height — in, cm or mm.Tells us the shipping bulk, and tells two cartons of one size apart.
Cost eachWhat that box cost you. Tip if there was one.It is what we settle with you against.
4Supplier: add a box

Tap Add boxes on the label you are packing, then for each box:

  1. Scan or type the SKU printed on the empty box. The shoe's name fills in. Scanning the UPC instead also fills in the size.
  2. Tap the size the box is for. Tap it again for a second box of that size, or use + Custom if the size is not listed.
  3. Enter the box dimensions — length × width × height, measured on the outside. Switch in to cm if that is what your tape reads.
  4. Enter the cost per box. Leave it blank if you genuinely do not know — blank means "not stated", which is not the same as free.
  5. Tap Add … to label.
One box, fully declared. The button stays greyed out until the size and all three dimensions are filled in.
5Supplier: check the list as it grows

Every box you add appears on the label with its size and its carton. You can correct any of it in place — tap a field, change it, tap away.

Three boxes on Label 1. Note the count reads “3 boxes”, not “3 units”.
Two boxes that become identical will merge If you correct a line so that its SKU, size and dimensions match another line, the two become one line with the quantities added together. That is on purpose — they are the same box.
6Supplier: one carton size across the whole list

Most orders are a run of sizes that all ship in the same carton. Type it once instead of thirty times.

  1. Tap Set box size for N lines under the list.
  2. Enter the dimensions.
  3. Choose Apply to all N, or Only the N still blank if you have already measured some by hand.
“Only the ones still blank” exists so a bulk apply can never overwrite a measurement you took deliberately.
Sizes are never touched Applying one carton across sizes 8, 9 and 10 leaves you three lines. Only the dimensions change.
7Supplier: review, close, print, attach, ship

Identical to a shoes order, and in the same order:

  1. Review & close box when the label is full. It becomes Ready to ship.
  2. Print the manifest on plain Letter paper. It now carries a BOX SIZE column beside the size, and totals in boxes.
  3. Attach it to the box, then seal it.
  4. Ship the label once the courier has taken the parcel.
Close one box at a time A label is closed and printed as a unit. Reopening a closed box invalidates a sheet you have already printed — so finish one, print it, attach it, and only then start the next.

If something is not right

What you seeWhat to do
“This order is for empty shoe boxes — give the box's length, width and height.”A size on its own is not a declaration. Fill in all three dimensions.
“Say which shoe size this box is for.”Tap a size chip, or + Custom if the size is not listed.
“This order is for shoes — a pair has a size, not box dimensions.”The order is still marked as a shoes order. Ask us to switch it (Step 2).
“Couldn't look up <SKU> — declaring it anyway.”Harmless. The catalogue only supplies the shoe's name here. Type the name and carry on.
The Add button is greyed outA row is missing its size or a dimension. The line just above the button says which.
You closed a box too earlyReopen it, fix it, close it again — and reprint the manifest. The old sheet is void.

The warehouse: counting them in

Same wizard as a shipment of shoes. What changes is what you count.

8Receive against the order
  1. Open Receive New and tap Receive against a purchase order.
  2. Find the order — scan the label on the parcel, or pick it from the open list. The Empty boxes chip tells you what is inside before you cut the tape.
  3. Tap Add items on the box you are opening.
The chip is on the picker, on the banner, and on every list — you never have to remember which order was which.
9Count what is actually in the carton

The screen is the supplier's own list, one row per size and carton. Nothing is pre-counted — a number nobody took is worse than no number.

  1. If the shipment is complete, tap Everything arrived as declared. One tap, not two hundred.
  2. Otherwise count each row in with the + / − stepper.
  3. A carton that is not on the list at all goes in with + Add unexpected — it will read as an overage, which is exactly what it is.
  4. Submit the box.
Each row is a size and the carton it ships in — the same shoe in two carton sizes is two rows, because they are two different things to count.
No stickers are printed Empty boxes get no 1ID label. A box's label is the shoe box label, printed from Box Labels when the carton finally goes on a pair.
10Settle it with the supplier

PO Reconciliation compares what was declared against what you counted, per shoe and size, and says so in boxes.

A clean shipment reads no difference and closes itself. This one is one carton short, and says which.
The reports are the same four What we received is the sheet to send a supplier when a box shipment is short; Discrepancies by box is the short version you carry back to the shelf.
11Shelve them, then find one when you need it
  1. Put them away with Shelve / Put-away, exactly like shoes. Boxes have their own To shelve count on the home screen so they never inflate the shoe backlog.
  2. When you want one, open Empty Box Stock and search by SKU or size — that is how the question gets asked: “is there a box for a 10.5 Panda?”
Grouped shoe → size → carton, with where they are sitting. Thirty identical boxes are one line, not thirty.

Putting a box on a pair

The reason all of this exists.

12Spend a box from the No Box queue

You do this from the pair, not from the stock screen — the No Box queue is the only place that knows which boxes fit.

  1. Open No Box / Not Ready and find the pair.
  2. Tap Use a box from stock. Only boxes matching that shoe and size are offered.
  3. Tap Use one.
Identical cartons on one shelf are a single choice. The oldest is taken, so stock rotates on its own.
What happens when you tap it The pair becomes With Box and drops out of this queue, ready to shelve and sell. The box is spent: it leaves the shelf, is marked Used on a pair, and both records carry the link. That is how “what happened to the forty boxes we bought” has an answer.
A box is spent once Used is final. A carton that has gone onto a shoe can never be shelved or handed out again — the same rule that stops a pair being sold twice.
If you sourced a box another way Use Box found → With Box instead. It makes the pair sellable without spending anything from stock, which keeps the count honest.

If something is not right — warehouse

What you seeWhat to do
The order isn't in the Receive against a purchase order listThe supplier hasn't shipped a label yet, or it's already reconciled. Search the tracking number to pull it up.
A row has no carton sizeThe supplier left it blank. Count it in anyway — the count is the point; the dimensions can be fixed on the order.
A carton in the parcel isn't on the list+ Add unexpected. It reads as an overage, which is the truth.
Use a box from stock says none in stockNothing on the shelf fits that shoe and size. Either order some, or use Box found if you have one from elsewhere.
Empty boxes in the shoe backlogThey aren't. Boxes have their own To shelve and On hand counts on the Empty Box Stock card.
The PH team asks about a box orderThey can't see one at all, by design — boxes are never priced or listed. Answer from Empty Box Stock.
